originality.rationale: An exact full temporal/orbit/individual-basin classification of the cuboctahedral graph and the 12-vertex 4-valent circulant under two-contact, three-state Greenberg--Hastings dynamics is not implied by the closest inspected published theorems. The immediate cuboctahedral three-periodic population is specifically acknowledged as covered by the prior proper Tait-coloring result, and a general balanced-coloring theorem covers the initial three-cycle mechanism. The new content lies in exact eventual basin spectra, sharp joint entry-time populations, and the circulant four-/six-cycle populations and exceptional basins. Explicit semantic comparisons and historical risks are recorded.
residual_risks: A specialized unpublished or unindexed exact small-graph dynamical table could already contain these populations.

The 2020 graph-class listing is a web account; although both supplied graphs are explicitly arc-transitive, an exhaustive uniqueness classification of all 12-vertex quartic graphs was not independently proved here.
The 2016 threshold-one paper was reviewed at abstract level, not through full text; this distinction in contact threshold is explicit in its stated model.
Independent external mathematical audit has not been performed.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of two explicit 12-vertex quartic arc-transitive graphs of sharply contrasting local geometry. It goes beyond covered period-three counts by showing one graph has 8 isolated three-cycle orbits and no oscillatory transient basin, while the other has 32 four-orbits and 2 six-orbits with exact basin sizes 180 and 12810, attracting 31386 states. The same maximum transient six on both isolates the influence of geometry on recurrence and basin organization rather than mere relaxation speed; it provides an exact, reusable finite benchmark. No infinite-family claim is needed.
